original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pushforward-injective-flat}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi.
If $f$ is flat, then $f_*\mathcal{I}$ is an injective
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-module
for any injective $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-module $\mathcal{I}$.

final_content.statement:
A *flat morphism of ringed topoi* $f$ has exact inverse-image on module categories (equivalently, its module pullback $f^*$ is exact). This flatness is asserted only here; it is not a standing hypothesis for the later Leray lemmas.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi.
If $f$ is flat, then $f_*\mathcal{I}$ is an injective
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-module
for any injective $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-module $\mathcal{I}$.
hypotheses: $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ is a **flat** morphism of ringed topoi.
$\mathcal I$ is an injective $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module.
conclusions: $f_*\mathcal I$ is an injective $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$-module.

semantic_review_note: For a FLAT ringed-topos morphism f, exactness of pullback makes pushforward of an injective O_C-module I into an injective O_D-module. The proposal explicitly does not inherit flatness into following Leray statements.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-Leray}
Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules. There is a spectral sequence
$$
E_2^{p, q} = H^p(\mathcal{D}, R^qf_*(\mathcal{F}^\bullet))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}^\bullet)$.

final_content.statement:
For a morphism of ringed topoi $f$, $Rf_*$ is the derived pushforward and $R^qf_*(\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is its $q$th cohomology sheaf. The groups $H^p(\mathcal D,-)$ and $H^{p+q}(\mathcal C,-)$ are derived global-sections cohomology; a bounded-below complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is assumed to ensure the indicated spectral sequence applies. There is **no flatness hypothesis** on $f$.

Let $f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules. There is a spectral sequence
$$
E_2^{p, q} = H^p(\mathcal{D}, R^qf_*(\mathcal{F}^\bullet))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}^\bullet)$.
hypotheses: $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ is an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi.
$\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a bounded-below complex of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-modules.
conclusions: There is a Leray spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(\mathcal D,R^q f_*(\mathcal F^\bullet))\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(\mathcal C,\mathcal F^\bullet)$.

semantic_review_note: A bounded-below complex of O_C-modules under an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi f admits the Leray spectral sequence H^p(D,R^q f_*F•) abutting H^{p+q}(C,F•); there is no flatness assumption.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-relative-Leray}
Let
$f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
and
$g : (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{E}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{E})$
be morphisms of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-module.
There is a spectral sequence with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = R^pg_*(R^qf_*\mathcal{F})
$$
converging to $R^{p + q}(g \circ f)_*\mathcal{F}$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$, and there
is a version for bounded below complexes of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules.

final_content.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be composable morphisms of ringed topoi, and let $R^q f_*$ and $R^p g_*$ denote their higher direct images. The spectral sequence computes the higher direct images of the composite $g\circ f$, not merely global cohomology. The same construction is asserted for bounded-below complexes in place of a single module.

Let
$f : (\Sh(\mathcal{C}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
and
$g : (\Sh(\mathcal{D}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}) \to
(\Sh(\mathcal{E}), \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{E})$
be morphisms of ringed topoi.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-module.
There is a spectral sequence with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = R^pg_*(R^qf_*\mathcal{F})
$$
converging to $R^{p + q}(g \circ f)_*\mathcal{F}$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$, and there
is a version for bounded below complexes of $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}$-modules.
hypotheses: $f:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ and $g:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal E),\mathcal O_{\mathcal E})$ are composable morphisms of ringed topoi.
conclusions: There is a spectral sequence of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal E}$-modules $E_2^{p,q}=R^p g_*(R^q f_*\mathcal F)\Rightarrow R^{p+q}(g\circ f)_*\mathcal F$, functorial in $\mathcal F$.
An analogous relative Leray spectral sequence exists for bounded-below complexes of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-modules.

semantic_review_note: For composable ringed-topos morphisms f and g, the spectral sequence of higher direct image sheaves R^p g_*(R^q f_*F)⇒R^{p+q}(g∘f)_*F is functorial in F, with the source's additional bounded-below-complex variant preserved.
